newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Sabanci Hldg foreign share offer oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Turk Sabanci Hldg foreign share offer oversubscribed.

text.p: Sabanci Holding, one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates, said its partial share offer of around $170 million met a demand of more than $260 million from investors in foreign markets.

"Our share sale in foreign markets has been successfully completed. A total demand of $263 million was received from more than 100 investors in 13 cities," Faruk Bilen, head of the Holding's capital markets department told a news conference.
"45 percent of the (foreign) demand came from 33 different funds in the U.S., 40 percent from 61 funds in Europe and 15 percent from five funds in Far East and Australia," he said.
Bilen added that 28 of the Europeans funds were based in England.
Sabanci Holding floated five billion shares at 5,400 lira fixed price per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share and allocated 4.5 billion, or 90 percent of it to foreigners.
The remaining 500 million shares will be sold to domestic investors in a two-day offer starting on Wednesday. 50 million of this offer will be allocated to local institutional investors.

The domestic offer will be lead managed by Turkiye Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi and co-managed by Ak securities, owned by Sabanci Holding's banking arm Akbank. 11 other members also participate in the consortium.

Sabanci Holding waived five trillion lira of preemptive rights to offer them to the public as part of its plan to double its capital to 50 trillion lira by issuing 14.6 trillion lira of bonuses and 10.4 trillion lira of rights.
